claims.text: The unmodified high-entropy alloy has not displayed superconductivity in the low-temperature regime.
Adding a small fraction of a superconducting element will enable superconductivity to emerge in the alloy at low temperature.
The added element will enhance local electron-phonon coupling.
The added element will reduce impurity scattering in the disordered lattice.
Niobium is an example of a known superconducting element suitable for the proposed addition.
Adding a few atomic percent of the selected element causes subtle local lattice modifications.
The compositional addition increases electron density in regions enriched with the superconducting element.
The proposed local lattice modifications and increased electron density strengthen electron-phonon interactions.
Stronger electron-phonon coupling supports Cooper-pair formation below a critical temperature.
Cooper-pair formation will produce a superconducting phase absent from the unmodified alloy.
The modified alloy is expected to show a marked drop in electrical resistance at low temperature.
The modified alloy is expected to exhibit a Meissner effect at low temperature.
The base alloy should remain non-superconducting under the same testing conditions.
The superconductivity-promoting effect should hold for additions in the low-to-moderate range of a few atomic percent.
Exceeding the proposed concentration range could destabilize the high-entropy phase.
Excessive addition could cause phase separation or other competing effects.
Uniform thermal annealing minimizes microstructural variations among the compared samples.
